Time-over 
 current relays are used for the protection of feeders, transmission lines, 
 alternating-current machines and transformers, and numerous other applications 
 where accurate measurement of current and timing is necessary.

To ensure 
 proper coordination with a minimum of circuit isolation, the operating time of 
 associated protective devices should be considered when selecting a 
 time-current characteristic for a particular application. Four basic 
 time-current characteristics are available for the MDP relay

Protection | Technical Procedure
Introduction
Time-over 
 current relays are used for the protection of feeders, transmission lines, 
 alternating-current machines and transformers, and numerous other applications 
 where accurate measurement of current and timing is necessary.
To ensure 
 proper coordination with a minimum of circuit isolation, the operating time of 
 associated protective devices should be considered when selecting a 
 time-current characteristic for a particular application. Four basic 
 time-current characteristics are available for the MDP relay

Work to be carried out
Relays Preparation
Review the manual and drawings.
Prepare the previous or commissioning results of the 
relay testing.
Check the wires of the relay by hand.
Check the AC source is available to the tester.
Check the existence of the DC sources in panels.
Disconnect the trip leads of the relay and connect one of 
them to the timer of the tester.
Check all the leads used in tests.
Test Steps
Connect the current leads of a tester unit to the relay points 
 according to the drawings and scheme.
Inject current to each couple of points till the red flag 
of the device displays.
Repeat the steps for each pair of points according to the 
test sheet.
Record the results.
Testing the Relay and Protection Outputs
Carefully follow these test procedure steps
Verify the test result match the relay setting. If not consult 
 technical services.
Test trip the circuit breaker associated with the relay.
Trip Test
Request the operator to switch on the main circuit breaker.
Operate the output auxiliary contact by injection to trip the 
 circuit breaker.
Check that the circuit breaker tripped.
Set the switch on the 
 front of the relay so the output relays correspond to phase or ground 
 (Position B)
 Connect the relay as indicated in 
 the figure below. In order to apply current to the relay, use a supply of 120 
 or 220 volts, 50/60HZ, with a variable resistor in series, or an electronic 
 test source.
